newsitem.title: USA: Salaries surging in emerging economies - Perrin.
newsitem.headline: Salaries surging in emerging economies - Perrin.

text.p: Salaries are soaring in some Latin American and Asian countries as booming local economies create a strong demand for skilled workers, a Towers Perrin study released Sunday showed.

In Venezuela, inflation has pushed average salaries up 80 percent or more this year for all categories of employees, the management consulting firm said. Pay levels in Brazil, China, Hong Kong, Mexico and South Africa are also growing at double digits.
By contrast, U.S. salaries are growing at three to four percent a year, the annual survey showed.

"While salary growth in 1997 is projected to slow somewhat in a few of these markets you would hardly call a 30 percent annual growth rate moderate -- at least by current U.S. standards," said Bob Freedman, a Towers Perrin principal. "Of course, most of these increases are due to inflationary economic environments and not growth in real wage levels."

CEOs in several countries earn far more than the average worker than in the U.S., Towers Perrin said. In Venezuela, for instance, a CEO earns 75 times more than a manufacturing employee, 44 times more in Mexico and 41 times more in Brazil.
